research_question: Does an ex-ante observable WIN/WDO cross-asset state provide stable out-of-sample economic expectation after costs, and does regime conditioning improve materially over a static inverse-correlation rule?

hypotheses.H_static: A static inverse WIN/WDO relationship has subsequent predictive economic value beyond contemporaneous correlation.
hypotheses.H_regime: The inverse relationship is regime-dependent and ex-ante observable regime conditioning improves out-of-sample economic performance versus the static rule.
hypotheses.H_break: The inverse relationship breaks or reverses in identifiable regimes; failure to survive long horizons and distinct regimes rejects the family.

promotion_rule: Promotion requires stable predictive power outside discovery, after costs, across materially distinct historical horizons/regimes, with a pre-specified ex-ante regime rule outperforming the static inverse benchmark without causal backfill. Otherwise reject.
rejection_rule: Reject if predictive power is absent out of sample, economics fail after costs, dependence is only contemporaneous, results are concentrated in one short regime/horizon, regime identification is not ex-ante observable, or regime-conditioned performance is not robustly superior to the static benchmark.
next_step_after_merge: Audit existing qualified WIN/WDO artifacts and frozen cost convention, then freeze exact horizons/splits/features/tests before reading this family's economic outcomes.
